sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः । स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
hindiTranslation: श्रीभगवान् बोले  कर्मफलका आश्रय न लेकर जो कर्तव्यकर्म करता है, वही संन्यासी तथा योगी है और केवल अग्निका त्याग करनेवाला संन्यासी नहीं होता तथा केवल क्रियाओंका त्याग करनेवाला योगी नहीं होता ॥
englishTranslation: One who performs the required action without taking shelter in the fruit of action is a renunciate and a yogi. Not one who merely gives up fire, and not one who merely stops acting.
essence: Renunciation means acting without needing to own the result.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Real renunciation is not escaping action. It is doing what must be done without clinging to the result.
simpleInsight: Do what must be done and stop leaning on the result.
detailedMeaning: Krishna begins by redefining renunciation for Arjuna, who is frozen before battle: it means acting without dependence on results, and abandoning action falls short of it. This verse sets the tone for the whole teaching on self-mastery.
modernRelevance: An accountant quits her job to escape office politics and finds the resentment came along with her. Krishna's sannyasi keeps working and drops dependence on results, which is harder and more honest than walking away.
translationLiteral: श्रीभगवानुवाच (the divine said) / अनाश्रितः (not taking refuge) / कर्मफलम् (fruit of action) / कार्यम् (what must be done) / कर्म (action) / करोति (does) / यः (who) / सः (that one) / संन्यासी (renunciate) / च (and) / योगी (yogi) / च (and) / न (not) / निरग्निः (without fire) / न (not) / च (and) / अक्रियः (one without action)
insight: Krishna's renunciant does the required work without leaning on its fruit; giving up the ritual fire is not enough.

quoteVariants.text: Do the work. Drop the reward. That is renunciation.
Renunciation is doing the work without clutching the result.
